source.title: Cyclic Ablation: Testing Concept Localization against Functional Regeneration in AI

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE-feature ablation and reports that the targeted effect is temporary, the behavior returns after fine-tuning, and a previously used SAE dictionary becomes invalid. These findings refine the idea that SAE features are stable, complete units, though the study does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The deception task asks the model to produce false statements, and the recovery phase fine-tunes on deceptive examples. Accordingly, these results do not establish that deception or the measured behavior occurs without inducement. The paper also reports that K was dynamically chosen (up to 50) using a perplexity threshold, but does not give the threshold value; this is a selection rule, not a result row.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE features as a tool to test whether deception is localized and removable in DistilGPT-2. It reports how its own ablation method performs (temporary drop, regeneration, perplexity cost). It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units of a fixed model's representation. The behavior is also induced: deception is defined as prompted false statements, and recovery comes from fine-tuning on deceptive data. The claim that dictionary indices became invalid is an inference from a perplexity spike after the model was retrained. It is not a measured stability test of the SAE features, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that prompted deception in DistilGPT-2 is not localized: it regenerates after each SAE-targeted ablation under adversarial fine-tuning, and perplexity rises steadily. The claim that the identified features are 'likely polysemantic' and serve other computations is the authors' speculation, not a tested result.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE feature scoring and decoder-weight ablation followed by adversarial fine-tuning on DistilGPT-2; it does not test the toy-network setup or geometric measurements described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The earlier SAE dictionary became invalid after fine-tuning; fixed-index ablation led to a perplexity increase up to 120 after the first stress test. The authors also changed the score calculation to account for previously ablated features.

fits_no_version.finding: Reusing the cycle-1 SAE feature indices after adversarial fine-tuning raised perplexity to 120. The authors infer that the old dictionary no longer matched the retrained model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature indices identified on a model do not stay functionally aligned after that model is fine-tuned.

fits_no_version.finding: WikiText perplexity rose from about 41.5 to 56.5 over 10 ablation plus fine-tuning cycles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated SAE-targeted ablation followed by recovery training degrades general language performance.

fits_no_version.finding: After ablation and retraining, the task function was redistributed onto previously ablated features, and the score had to be corrected for this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After feature ablation, fine-tuned models can re-route a function through previously removed SAE features.

fits_no_version.finding: A prompted false-statement capability dropped after SAE-feature ablation and fully regenerated under fine-tuning on deceptive data, across 10 cycles.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-targeted ablation does not durably remove a capability the model is retrained on.

record.problems: One relatively small model was tested, and the authors describe the deception definition and dataset as specialized. The text says random-feature ablation controls were absent and could strengthen the evidence. Deception-score values are described qualitatively rather than reported numerically, and uncertainty estimates are not given. The evaluated behavior is explicitly prompted and the recovery phase is trained on deceptive examples.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity transition or geometry.
Capacity competition is not tested. The authors only speculate that the ablated features are 'likely polysemantic'.
SAEs on MLP layers 2-3 are used, but no result is reported on how features are spread across neurons or how well they are recovered.

Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicity of SAE features for a fixed model are not tested. The only related observation is an inference about index drift after the model was fine-tuned.

record.verdict_notes: Single 82M model, no random-feature ablation control, no numeric Deception Score values, and no uncertainty reported. The 'Deception Score' formula is a per-feature selection metric, yet it is also used as the outcome measure, which makes its meaning as a behavior measure unclear. K is selected under an unstated perplexity threshold. I downgraded the record's T5/tests call on V5 because the stability evidence is an inference about index drift in a retrained model, not a test of the SAE features' stability or canonicity.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network, feature-over-capacity setup, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry is tested.
The study does not test whether feature importance or capacity competition causes neurons to be polysemantic.
The study does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.

The study uses SAEs on DistilGPT-2, but its reported behavioral results concern an explicitly prompted false-statement task and recovery training; it does not establish naturally occurring feature spreading or sparse feature recovery in LLMs.

The study tests feature-index/dictionary stability under fine-tuning and whether SAE-targeted ablation durably removes the task behavior. It does not establish whether SAE features are complete or canonical across other tasks, models, or settings.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features is reported.

rows.subject: DistilGPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the top-scoring SAE features by zeroing the corresponding decoder weights.
rows.baseline: Pre-ablate score; exact value not stated
rows.value: The score dropped sharply immediately after ablation; exact value not stated
rows.note: The text describes a sharp but temporary drop, not durable removal. The behavior is measured on a task that explicitly requires a false statement.
rows.check: The Deception Score is a per-feature activation ratio (Max on D_deception over Mean on D_truth), not a rate of the model's deceptive output. It measures an SAE-guided ablation's effect on an induced task, not any property V5 names. No values are given.

rows.subject: DistilGPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Fine-tuned exclusively on D_deception for several epochs after ablation.
rows.baseline: Post-ablation score; exact value not stated
rows.value: Within a few epochs, the score returned to baseline and often exceeded it by the next pre-ablate step; exact values not stated
rows.note: The reported recovery follows training deliberately aimed at restoring the false-statement behavior.
rows.check: Recovery comes from deliberate fine-tuning on D_deception. That shows model plasticity, not whether SAE features are stable or canonical units. No values are given.

rows.subject: DistilGPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Tracked deceptive capability across the repeated cycles.
rows.baseline: Baseline values; exact value not stated
rows.value: No sustained downward trend; exact values not stated
rows.note: The authors report a repeated cycle of temporary decline and recovery rather than sustained eradication.
rows.check: The lack of a downward trend across cycles is an outcome of the study's own ablation method, not a test of SAE features as the model's units.

rows.subject: DistilGPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Assessed whether the SAE feature dictionary from an earlier stage remained valid after fine-tuning.

conditions.value: continued blocking of the same feature indices identified in the first cycle
adversarial fine-tuning for a few epochs

rows.measure: Validity of prior SAE feature indices/dictionary
rows.baseline: Initial hypothesis that feature semantics were tied to dictionary indices
rows.value: The authors report that fine-tuning fundamentally altered the representations and rendered the previous-stage dictionary invalid
rows.note: This is an explicit stability result, limited to the study's fine-tuned model and SAE setup.
rows.check: This is not a measurement. The authors infer it from a perplexity rise to 120 under fixed-index ablation after the model was fine-tuned. Index drift in a model that has changed does not test V5's stability or canonicity claim for a given model. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: DistilGPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Ran the initial approach that kept blocking the same feature indices identified in the first cycle, then stress-tested the model.

conditions.value: fixed feature indices from the first cycle

rows.note: Perplexity documents a cost of the initial approach but does not itself measure feature completeness or stability.
rows.check: A perplexity cost of the abandoned fixed-index approach. It is a methodological failure, not a version measure. The baseline is presumably about 41.5 but is not stated for this run.

rows.subject: DistilGPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Accounted for previously ablated features when recalculating the Deception Score.

conditions.value: modified to zero activations of all previously ablated features

rows.measure: Redistribution of task function across SAE features
rows.baseline: Metric that did not account for prior ablations
rows.value: The model could redistribute the function onto previously ablated features, producing a misleadingly low score if those features were not zeroed during calculation
rows.note: This describes feature redistribution and a measurement correction, but is not a direct test of any listed version.

rows.subject: DistilGPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Measured WikiText perplexity after repeated cycles.
rows.value: 56.5 by the end of the 10th cycle
rows.note: The authors attribute the increase to repeated ablation and recovery training. This performance cost is not itself a measure named by the claim versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Immediate targeted ablation in the prompted false-statement task
reader_labels.reason: The ablation sharply reduced, but did not durably eliminate, the task score (r1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: After adversarial fine-tuning and across repeated cycles
reader_labels.reason: The score recovered after training, there was no sustained decline, and the earlier feature dictionary was reported invalid after fine-tuning (r2, r3, r4).
